Subject: Launch readiness & signature queue — Avalon Health

Hi Evelyn / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great alignment. Attached is the first draft of the mutual action checklist (Avalon_MAP_v1.xlsx) pulled from our notes. Summary below and a proposed next-step cadence so we can lock the close and target go-live.

Key milestones (high level):
- Contract finalization (Redwood: send DocuSign draft) — target: 2026-08-27
- Security evidence delivered (Redwood: SOC2 summary) — target: 2026-08-13
- Network & SSO readiness (Avalon: provide IP ranges, certs) — target: 2026-08-24
- Sandbox testing & quality gates (joint) — target: 2026-08-31
- Production go-live — target week of 2026-09-06

Responsibilities (proposed):
- Redwood: provide SOC2 summary, deployment checklist, DocuSign contract, on-call for sandbox validation (Priyom + engineering).
- Avalon: approve MAP, provide procurement/PO timing, share network ACLs and SSO metadata, sign DocuSign when ready.

Dependencies & risks:
- If procurement PO is delayed > 10 business days after DocuSign, go-live could slip one sprint.
- For lowest latency we recommend Dedicated capacity; if Avalon prefers Private deployment there is a longer lead time for on-prem planning.

Attachments: Avalon_MAP_v1.xlsx (attachment).

Could you please:
1) Confirm the responsibilities above or propose edits;
2) Confirm whether the target go-live week of Sep 6 is acceptable;
3) Confirm who will be the signer for the DocuSign envelope (name + email).

I can get SOC2 summary and DocuSign draft over by Wednesday. Once we have your sign-off we’ll circulate MAP v2.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — good recap. Quick questions from our side:

1) Data residency: Avalon has a new EU tenant requirement for PHI-adjacent PII. Can you confirm whether the hosted option can be scoped to a specific region or whether we would need Private?
2) Can you send the SOC2 report or an executive summary (we only need high-level controls for procurement)?

Also: internal patching for our core platform is scheduled the week of Aug 30 which makes Sept 6 a little tight for go-live. If signature is completed by Aug 27 we can aim for Sep 13 as a safer production start. Would Redwood be able to support that shift if needed?

Evelyn

Hi Evelyn — quick technical follow-up and clarifications (pulling the answers from our notes):

- Data residency: Our hosted deployment supports region pinning for Dedicated clusters (we can pin to eu-west-1 for production). Private/on-prem is also available but requires more lead time. For PHI workflows we usually recommend Dedicated in-region or Private with customer-managed KMS.

- SOC2: attaching SOC2-summary.pdf (control scope, last audit date, remediation commitments). This should be sufficient for procurement screening; we can provide the full report under an NDA if needed.

- Network/SSO dependencies (what Avalon needs to provide):
  * IP ranges for inbound ACLs (we provide a recommended list)
  * SAML metadata for SSO integration
  * Service account for log ingestion (if you want audit streaming)

- Deployment recommendation: start with Dedicated (regional) for faster onboarding; evaluate Private later if compliance requires.

Updated milestone notes (proposed):
- SOC2 summary delivered: 2026-08-13 (done, attached)
- DocuSign contract sent: target 2026-08-20
- Contract signed: target 2026-08-27
- Sandbox testing window: 2026-08-31 — 2026-09-03
- Production go-live: 2026-09-13 (per Avalon preference)

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (attachment).

Subject: Updated MAP v2, contract redlines accepted, next steps

Hi all,

Thanks Priyom — that helps. I’ve incorporated the technical notes and Avalon’s preferred timeline into MAP v2 and circulated the contract with the negotiated redlines accepted by legal. Attachments: Avalon_MAP_v2.xlsx, Contract_Redlines_accepted.pdf (both attached).

Callouts in the update:
- Success criteria (draft):
  1) p95 latency < 100ms for typical request size (verified in sandbox)
  2) 99.9% platform availability SLA for the Dedicated cluster
  3) Token cost under $0.0008 per token for steady-state throughput (billing model to be finalized in contract)
- Acceptance test plan: 3-day sandbox soak (API traffic profile), functional regression suite, and an on-call test window where Redwood engineers will validate KV cache and streaming performance.

Marissa — can you confirm the success criteria wording and acceptance gate so we can send to procurement as the final criteria?

Next steps:
1) Avalon to confirm signer + PO timing;
2) Redwood to send DocuSign envelope (target 8/20);
3) Joint sandbox test window scheduling (target week of 8/31).

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Subject: Re: Updated MAP v2, contract redlines accepted, next steps

All — I reviewed the success criteria and acceptance gates. Proposed final wording below (feel free to copy into the MAP):

Final acceptance criteria (to be met in sandbox and validated before production):
- Performance: p95 request latency < 100ms for representative payloads measured over a 72-hour soak (joint validation).
- Reliability: 99.9% uptime over a 30-day post-go-live window (monitored by Redwood Console).
- Functional: All critical regression tests pass (list in MAP v2) and no high-severity issues outstanding at sign-off.
- Cost: Billing model confirmed in contract and cost-per-token target <= $0.0008 for committed throughput.

Test plan summary: 72-hour sandbox soak + targeted load tests for peak traffic, one smoke-run with production-like keys, and a pair of success sign-off meetings (engineering + product) after the soak.

If that looks good to Avalon, we need their explicit sign-off (name + email) so procurement can accept DocuSign terms and kick the PO.

Marissa Cole
